rationale: M59 (#861), javascript half, CURRENT for the #868 round. This grammar nests decorators INSIDE the declaration (unlike typescript, where a method decorator is a class_body sibling) and does it for classes, fields AND methods — measured: class_declaration [decorator@32, class@33, ...], field_definition [decorator@34, property_identifier@35, ...], method_definition [decorator@37, property_identifier@38, ...]. So all three symbols and their `contains` lines named the decorator's line; fixed by skipping leading decorator children in nodeToRange, the same rule as typescript and scala (scala/declaration-lines-825) — that RANGE contract is unchanged and still pinned here. What CHANGED in this file at #868 is the decorator-ATTRIBUTION half, which this fixture deliberately left unpinned when the analyzer could not do it: it pinned `uses Service -> sealed` (32) and `uses method -> sealed` (37) as the only member-scoped trace of a decorator, with the rationale saying the metadata contract was measured and filed separately. #868 landed that contract, so those two rows are now the WRONG answer and have moved to forbidRelationships: a decorator's name is a `references` edge from the decorated symbol at the decorator's own line (the family rule — typescript's inDecoratorPosition, JVM annotations as metadata, the python oracle's PYD1), and the bare-read `uses` spelling is exactly what that rule deletes. The three `references` rows are added as expected, including the FIELD's (34) — the field path called no decorator collector at all before #868. Discriminating either way: re-adding the `uses` spelling fails against the forbid list, and losing the `references` edge fails against the expected list. 2026-10-18 CANONICAL VOCABULARY: the three decorator rows are now `decorates` (src/ast/types.ts landed RelationshipType.Decorates in df5a03eb2), not `references` — one row per decorator, source = the decorated declaration, target = the decorator name leaf, line = the decorator's own line. The near-miss forbid moved with them.
